# parity-fuzz --mode prompt baseline: normalized signatures of KNOWN gaps.
# A divergence whose signature is here is allowed; a NEW one fails CI.
# Regenerate: parity-fuzz --mode prompt --count N --verify 3  (copy NEW-signature lines).
#
# No known gaps — 4000 cases run clean. Covers the `print -P` / ${(%)…} prompt
# expander: %-escapes, %(x.t.f) ternaries, %N<s< / %N>s> truncation (BOTH
# signs), colours, and %{raw%} spans.
#
# Every divergence this mode found was a real port bug and was FIXED:
#
#   1. `%G` did not exist. There was no `G` arm in putpromptchar's escape
#      dispatch at all, so it fell to the unknown-escape default and emitted
#      nothing. c:Src/prompt.c:684-694 emits Nularg — a marker that prints
#      nothing but that countprompt charges ONE column (c:1183-1184 `else if
#      (*str == Nularg) w++;`). That is the whole purpose of the escape: telling
#      the expander that something invisible still occupies a cell.
#      Nothing downstream was at fault — countprompt already had its Nularg arm,
#      and prompttrunc already measures with countprompt (c:1343) — there was
#      simply never a Nularg in the buffer to count. So every truncation spent
#      the invisible column on a real character:
#          %5<<abcdefghij%G  → zsh `ghij` (4 visible + 1 for %G)   was `fghij`
#          %3<<abcdefg%G     → zsh `fg`                            was `efg`
#          %5<...<abcdefg%G  → zsh `...g`                          was `...fg`
#      and `%G%(1l.t.f)` took the false branch where zsh takes the true one.
#
#   2. The `%{` → `%G` FALLTHROUGH (c:676-683) was missing with it. C runs the
#      two as one case: `%{` pushes Inpar, and then `if (arg <= 0) break;` —
#      so a COUNTED `%N{…%}` continues into the Nularg emission and claims N
#      columns, while a plain `%{…%}` claims none. `%3{xy%}%(3l.t.f)` must be
#      true; it was false.
#
#   3. `%-N<` / `%-N>` (negative truncation width) did not truncate. c:663-672
#      reads `-N` as "N columns before the RIGHT MARGIN" — `arg = zterm_columns
#      - t0 + arg`, then c:670-671 clamps a non-positive result to 1 — not as a
#      literal width. Two port bugs hid behind that one symptom:
#        - prompt.rs invented an 80-column terminal (`if cols <= 0 {cols = 80}`)
#          for a shell that has none, so the clamp-to-1 never fired. Not in the
#          C, which reads the zterm_columns global and lets it be 0. Same
#          invention sat on the `%(Nl.t.f)` path (c:461-462).
#        - zshrs never called adjustwinsize(0) at init (c:Src/init.c:1276), so
#          $COLUMNS/$LINES read 0 even at a real terminal — which is what made
#          that fake 80 load-bearing. In a 97x24 pty zsh reports 97/24 and
#          zshrs reported 0/0.
#      Both are fixed; the generator now emits negative widths from the same
#      vocabulary as positive ones, and reverting either fix makes this mode
#      fail — the property that makes the gate worth having.
#
# ~12% of generated cases TIME OUT, and they are ZSH hanging, not zshrs. The
# harness drops zsh-side timeouts (`if !z.timed_out && differs(...)`), so they
# are uncomparable rather than wrong. It is an upstream infinite loop in
# countprompt's line-wrap loop:
#     while (w > zterm_columns && overf >= 0 && !multi) {
#         h++;
#         if (wcw) { w = wcw; break; }
#         else { w -= zterm_columns; }     /* w -= 0 → spins forever */
#     }
# With zterm_columns == 0 the subtraction never terminates. It needs ALL of: a
# styled span with CONTENT (`%B x %b`, `%U..%u`, `%S..%s`, `%F{red}..%f`; an
# empty `%B%b` is fine), then the `l` conditional (not `L`, not `j`), a real
# TERM (xterm/vt100 hang; dumb/empty/unknown do not), and COLUMNS == 0. zshrs
# does not hang — its countprompt guards the zero case. Do NOT "fix" this by
# exporting COLUMNS from the harness: COLUMNS == 0 is exactly the regime the
# `%-N<` gap lived in, and papering over it would retire the coverage that
# found it.
#
# UNKNOWN conditional test char `%(X.T.F)` (fixed in prompt.rs): the ternary
# vocabulary only carried VALID test chars, so an unknown one was never
# compared. c:Src/prompt.c:501-503 sets `default: test = -1`, and the two
# branch calls fire on `test == 1` / `test == 0` respectively — so with -1
# NEITHER prints and `%(a.Y.N)` collapses to empty. The port left `test = 0`,
# wrongly emitting the FALSE branch `N`. The same edit ported the `t/T/d/D/w`
# clock tests (c:414-438, `arg == localtime field`) which had also fallen into
# that default arm. Reverting the default to `test = 0` yields 126 divergences
# on seed 1 alone (verified), so `%(a.Y.N)` / `A%(z.Y.N)B` / `%(q...)` /
# `%(Q...)` now gate it. The clock tests are NOT generated (nondeterministic).
#
# Any divergence here is a regression.
